answers.text: This happens a lot with our suppliers so I know the pattern. I would say: read the email and always give me exactly three lines in this order — first the delivery date, second the item and quantity, third what has changed compared to the original order. Keep each line short, one sentence. If you do this every time the same way, it will always come out the same.
Same idea as before. Tell the AI: make a memo with these fields — date, amount, category, submitter — always in this order. That way everyone's memo looks the same.

I read this twice because something did not fit. The call was on the 14th, they say delivery moved to the 19th, but then it says 'three days out from today' — that does not work together. The price part, 100 times 48.50, is fine, no problem there. Before this goes to the client, I would double-check the dates are right.

Numbers here: 62 up from 54, that part is fine, about 15% up, matches. But then '3 late out of 62 is 97%' — that's not right, 3 out of 62 is more like 95%, not 97%. I would go back and check this rate before it goes up the chain.

I would sign off Output 2, because it shows the actual numbers, 25,100 and 612,000, so I can see where 4.1% came from. Output 1 just gives the percent, no numbers behind it, so I don't know how they got it.
I would send Reply 2, it has the order number and credit reference, looks more solid to me.

1. Customer's delivery address — no, that's personal detail about the customer, would not paste that in. 2. Sales figure total — I think this is fine, it's just a number. For the others I am not one hundred percent sure, would need to ask my manager first before pasting company pricing or a colleague's number in there.
The pricing and discount numbers I would not paste in, feels too sensitive for a tool we have not cleared yet. The rest I am less sure, would maybe ask first.
Before it goes to my manager, I would compare the total deliveries number against my own list from that week. This is quick, so I do this always before sending.

Step 4 is the one that worries me most, because it sends the confirmation automatically without anyone looking. But also step 1, because if the AI reads the order wrong at the start, that mistake carries through the rest without anyone noticing. I would put a check before step 4, so someone looks at it first.
